name: Glasses frame selection by face shape

lead: This is the idea that certain frame shapes flatter certain face shapes, sometimes pitched as a way to look more angular or add a 'hunter eyes' impression.
No studies were found testing it, and reference sources on glasses discuss lens and frame types rather than face-shape rules.

paras: Frame lines, colour and size are said to contrast or echo facial features and shift where the eye is drawn.
No health risks. Frames that fit poorly can be uncomfortable; effects on appearance are subjective.

lead: Glasses frame selection by face shape is a style practice in which people pick frame shapes intended to balance or complement their face, for example choosing frames to add a perceived 'hunter eyes' look. Wikipedia notes that people often choose frames based on how they look on the wearer.[1]
The Wikipedia article on glasses does not discuss face shape and no studies were found testing whether matching frames to face shape changes perceived attractiveness.

paras: Frame styles include aviator, browline, horn-rimmed, rimless, Wayfarer and others, made from plastics, metals and natural materials.[1] Higher-power lenses tend to suit smaller, rounder frames to limit distortion and weight.[1]
Glasses were once stigmatised in some eras, and public figures and designers later helped make them fashion accessories.[1]
Appearance communities discuss frame shape as a way to alter the perceived eye area or balance jaw and face width. No community sources were available to quote.
